body.statement: Using the finite-risk saddle handle, characterize the dosage in \(\mathcal D_L\) minimizing the worst-case unconditional risk of the specified spectral-threshold OLS estimator over \(\|\beta\|_2\le B\) and the admissible conditional-noise class. Determine an explicit finite-\(n\) frontier separating regimes in which \(d^\star\) is minimax from regimes in which a nonuniform independent dosage has strictly smaller worst-case risk.
body.justification: Population \(A\)-optimality does not settle the discontinuous finite-sample risk created by missing patterns and fallback bias.
body.gap: ShyamalZhangUhler2025 proves only near-optimal bounds, and DerezinskiWarmuth2017 obtains exact inverse-Gram identities under a different dependent sampling law.
body.consumer: The frontier would tell small interaction screens whether the asymptotically optimal uniform dosage is also the correct finite-budget design.
